memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"On the first day of the third month after the Israelites left Egypt-on that very
day-they came to the Desert of Sinai. After they set out from Rephidim, they
entered the Desert of Sinai, and Israel camped there in the desert in front of
the mountain." - Ex 19:1-2 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
They have arrived. Three months out of Egypt, and here is the mountain.

This is the place where it all began for Moses. Forty years earlier he stood at
this very mountain watching a bush burn, and God said something remarkable to
him: "When you have brought the people out of Egypt, you will worship God on
this mountain" (Ex 3:12).

That was the sign God gave. Not a sign Moses could verify beforehand, but one he
would only recognise afterwards. Moses had to obey first and see the
confirmation later.

Now here they are. The whole nation, camped in front of the mountain where the
bush burned.

God keeps His word, but often the proof arrives after the obedience rather than
before it. That is a hard order for us. We would prefer confirmation first and
commitment second.

Notice the small phrase "on that very day." Exodus keeps drawing attention to
exact timing. God is not vague about dates. What He said would happen happened,
and the narrator wants us to see it.

If you are waiting for confirmation before you obey, this verse gently suggests
the sequence may run the other way.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Are you waiting for proof before you obey something God has made clear?
2. Where has God brought you that you could not have foreseen?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Father, You keep Your word exactly. Give me courage to obey before I see the
confirmation. Amen.
